originalTitle: Bill Miller's investing strategy: How the legendary fund manager outperformed the market for 15 straight years
simplifiedContent: Bill Miller, a well-known fund manager, was able to beat the stock market for 15 years in a row. He did this by using a strategy that combines finding undervalued companies, being patient, and going against the crowd. Miller looks for companies with strong finances and a "margin of safety" to protect his investments, and he holds onto stocks until they reach a fair price or his reason for investing changes. This approach allowed him to outperform the S&P 500, a common measure of the overall stock market. By following this strategy, Miller was able to achieve impressive results and prove himself as a skilled investor.

originalTitle: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank posts Rs 34 crore Q1 loss; asset quality stress persists
simplifiedContent: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank lost Rs 34 crore in the first quarter of the year, which is the fifth time in a row they've reported a loss. This means the bank didn't make a profit, but instead lost money. The main reason for this loss is that many of the bank's loans are not being paid back, which is known as "asset quality stress". The bank's bad loans, or "gross non-performing assets", are still very high at 6.1%, which is a concern. This loss matters because it shows that the bank is still facing significant challenges in getting its loans paid back, which can affect its overall financial health.

originalTitle: Muthoot Finance reports 25% rise in Q1 profit, announces leadership transition
simplifiedContent: Muthoot Finance, a company that lends money to people using their gold as security, made a profit of Rs 2,550 crore in the first quarter of the year. This is 25% more than they made during the same time last year. The company's gold loan business is doing very well, which is why their profit is up. The company is also making some changes at the top, with Alexander George Muthoot set to become the new managing director on October 1, if the shareholders agree. This news matters because it shows that Muthoot Finance is doing well and making more money, which could be good for people who have invested in the company.

originalTitle: Yen Traders Brace for More Intervention With US at Japan’s Side
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: Japan and the US worked together last week to try to strengthen the Japanese yen, and now traders are waiting to see if they'll do it again. This means that Japan and the US took actions to try to increase the value of the yen compared to other currencies. Traders are watching closely because this can affect the stock market and economies. When Japan and the US intervene like this, it can have a big impact on the value of the yen, which is why traders are on "high alert" for more intervention. This could happen again when trading starts in Asia on Monday.

originalTitle: Wall Street’s Favorite Bet Comes Undone as Chips Whipsaw Market
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: many investors on Wall Street had been betting heavily on stocks related to computer chips, which had been doing very well. However, this trend is now reversing, causing a lot of uncertainty and swings in the market. This is because investors are getting worried that the current high level of spending on artificial intelligence might not continue. As a result, the market is experiencing a lot of volatility, which can be unsettling for investors. This matters because it could affect the overall direction of the stock market and the value of investments.

originalTitle: Banks Offload Risk from Leveraged ETFs With Exotic ‘Crash Puts’
simplifiedContent: There are investment products called leveraged ETFs that try to give investors double or triple the daily returns of a single stock. However, these products are very risky for the people who buy them. Some banks that sell these leveraged ETFs are trying to reduce their own risk by using special protection called "crash puts". This means they are taking steps to limit their potential losses if the investments perform poorly. This matters because it shows that even the banks that sell these risky products are aware of their potential downsides and are taking measures to protect themselves.
